description:
The Continuation of Pension scheme, also known as the K.B.O.C.W.W.B, was launched by the Government of India in 2019. 

This scheme is specifically designed to provide financial assistance to the families of deceased workers in the unorganized sector. 

The primary objective of the K.B.O.C.W.W.B scheme is to ensure that the families of workers who have lost their lives while engaged in work receive a pension. 

This pension aims to provide a safety net for the dependents of these workers, ensuring their financial stability during difficult times. 

The scheme targets the families of workers who are registered under the Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996. 

The pension amount provided under this scheme is ₹3,000 per month. 

This amount is intended to support the family in meeting their basic needs and maintaining a standard of living after the loss of the primary breadwinner. 

The eligibility criteria for this scheme are specific and must be met to qualify for the pension. 

The applicant must be a dependent family member of a registered construction worker who has died due to any cause. 

The age limit for the applicants is typically set at 18 years and above. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required to apply for this pension scheme. 

However, the applicant must provide proof of their relationship to the deceased worker. 

The application process for the K.B.O.C.W.W.B scheme involves several steps. 

First, the applicant must obtain the application form, which can be downloaded from the official website of the Ministry of Labour and Employment. 

Next, the applicant must fill out the form with accurate details regarding their identity and relationship to the deceased worker. 

The applicant must also gather necessary documents, including the death certificate of the worker. 

Additionally, proof of the applicant's identity such as an Aadhaar card or voter ID is required. 

Once the form is completed and documents are gathered, the applicant must submit the application to the local office of the Labour Department. 

The application can also be submitted online through the official portal if available in the respective state. 

After submission, the application will be reviewed by the concerned authorities. 

The timeline for processing the application can vary but generally takes around 30 days from the date of submission. 

If the application is approved, the pension will be disbursed monthly to the eligible beneficiary. 

The pension is typically credited directly to the bank account of the beneficiary. 

It is important for the beneficiary to have a bank account linked to their Aadhaar number for seamless transactions. 

The K.B.O.C.W.W.B scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Labour and Employment. 

Each state has its own Labour Department that oversees the implementation of this scheme at the local level. 

The contact details for the Ministry of Labour and Employment can be found on their official website. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to improve the welfare of workers in the unorganized sector. 

According to the 2011 Census, there are approximately 44 crore workers in the unorganized sector in India. 

This sector includes construction workers, agricultural laborers, and domestic workers among others. 

The K.B.O.C.W.W.B scheme is crucial in providing financial support to the families of these workers. 

In recent years, the government has emphasized the importance of social security for unorganized workers. 

The scheme aims to reduce poverty and improve the living standards of the families affected by the loss of a breadwinner. 

The pension amount of ₹3,000 is a significant support considering the economic challenges faced by many families in India. 

The government has also launched awareness campaigns to ensure that eligible families are informed about the scheme. 

These campaigns aim to educate families on how to apply and the benefits they can receive. 

The K.B.O.C.W.W.B scheme is a step towards recognizing the contributions of workers in the unorganized sector. 

It acknowledges the risks they face and the need for social security measures. 

The scheme is expected to benefit thousands of families across the country. 

The government has made provisions to ensure that the funds allocated for this scheme are utilized effectively. 

Regular audits and assessments are conducted to monitor the implementation of the scheme. 

This ensures that the benefits reach the intended beneficiaries without any delays or corruption. 

The K.B.O.C.W.W.B scheme is part of the government's larger vision of providing social security to all workers in India. 

It aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals set by the United Nations, particularly Goal 1 which aims to end poverty in all its forms everywhere. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to improving the welfare of its citizens. 

In conclusion, the K.B.O.C.W.W.B scheme is a vital initiative that provides financial assistance to the families of deceased construction workers. 

With a monthly pension of ₹3,000, it aims to alleviate the economic burden faced by these families. 

The eligibility criteria and application process are straightforward, ensuring that those in need can access the benefits easily. 

The implementation of the scheme by the Ministry of Labour and Employment reflects the government's dedication to social welfare. 

Through this scheme, the government aims to create a more secure and supportive environment for the families of workers in the unorganized sector.
